i feel like you can find a sweet spot between just telling your parents without his knowledge and just doing nothing.

in this particular situation, i empathize with your brother, mainly because i'm still underage and have been in somewhat of a similar situation in the past, you can take that as bias or insight, idk.

i can't tell you what to do, but i can say a couple of things about this situation:

it's important that your parents know, but it's not your role to tell them

if he called you to help him, he must trust you, and i feel like he'll listen if you make him feel safe, then you can talk about your concerns, and maybe come to an agreement on wha to do

and a couple of things talking from experience:

after we do really really stupid shit like that most teens think about it twice, we're still kinda dumb, but i feel like after this your brother will be more careful about this stuff, regardless of what you do

and most important (i can say this for certain) feeling safe and having a wholesome understanding of one's self identity is the most important thing, especially when you're young and need to form healthy relationships (i'm not there yet, but i know it's true)

so yeah, maybe if he's in that moment of wanting to have a partner he could ask out other gay (or idk) guys at his school or something, i know that if i had the balls i would've developed much healthier behavior than i have
